title: The tools, read whole (Rule of Benedict 4)
hookLine: the full list of seventy-some tools of good works
tomorrow: how much should God be loved? who would dare name an amount?

cards: Losing a borrowed tool on your first day has its own sinking feeling. Gregory the Great tells of a Goth, a newcomer at Benedict's monastery, handed a hooked blade to clear brambles beside a lake.
He swings hard, the iron flies off the handle, and it sinks out of sight. He's left holding a stick, and he runs to own up, shaking. In Benedict's house, tools mattered.
So what does the abbot do?

teach.b: Benedict takes the handle, holds it in the water, and the blade comes back up onto it. He hands it over with a few words: here, work, and don't be sad. No lecture.
The tool goes back into the newcomer's hands. That's the spirit of chapter four of Benedict's Rule, where he hangs a whole wall of what he calls the tools of good works. First, the big two.

Love the Lord God with all your heart, all your soul, all your strength, and your neighbor as yourself. Second, the hands. Relieve the poor, clothe the naked, visit the sick, bury the dead, console the grieving.
Right beside them: prefer nothing to the love of Christ. Third, the heart and the tongue.
Don't act on anger, don't nurse a grudge, pray for your enemies, make peace with someone before the sun goes down. Fourth, the last tool and the workshop.
The list ends: never despair of God's mercy.

Then Benedict says where the tools get used. The workshop is the enclosure of the monastery and stability in the community: staying put with the same people. Tools get dropped there, like the Goth's blade.
The Rule's answer is the abbot's: pick it up, and back to work.

how: Benedictine monks and nuns read a portion of the Rule every day, and many lay Catholics, called oblates, follow it in ordinary life.

o: Benedict's list of good works, used in community
a set of punishments for monks who broke the Rule
the farm equipment every monastery had to own

p: sank in the lake and came back

s: a monk's rule is mostly a list of chores and restrictions
chapter four lists good works as tools, starting with love of God and neighbor.
the last tool on Benedict's list is never despair of God's mercy
the list ends there, and then names the workshop.
in Gregory's story, Benedict punishes the newcomer for losing the blade
he brings it back and hands it over: work, and don't be sad.

games.q: your roommate keeps breaking your things by accident and keeps apologizing. you're about to say "whatever, I'm done." what's Benedict's move?
o: hand it back: fix what you can, and say keep going.
keep a list of every broken thing, for later.
ask for separate shelves so you never share again.
games.why: Benedict's tools are used in one workshop, with the same people. when the Goth lost the blade, the abbot gave it back: work, and don't be sad.

practice: If you have the Rule of Benedict nearby, or on your phone, open chapter four and read it straight through, slowly, without stopping to grade yourself. If not, hold four tools from today: love, help, make peace, never despair.
Notice which one your hands reach for first.

wordCard.voice: The tools. Benedict's wall of good works, used in one workshop: a community you stay with.

orig.note: Latin for tools: Benedict's word for the good works in chapter four.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: tools for the workshop, dropped sometimes and handed back. See you tomorrow.
